recipes.title: Paella Valenciana (Chicken & Shrimp)
recipes.dish_alt: A pan of golden saffron paella valenciana studded with chicken, shrimp, and peas
recipes.prep_alt: A wide paella pan simmering over an open flame as the saffron-infused rice cooks

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Chicken thighs, bone-in, cut into pieces
Large shrimp, peeled and deveined, tail-on

sections.heading: Steps
items: Steep the saffron threads in 2 tablespoons of warm stock for 10 minutes to bloom their color and aroma.
Season the chicken with salt and brown it in olive oil in a wide paella pan 6-8 minutes, turning once, until deeply golden. Remove to a plate.
In the same pan, cook the onion, garlic, and red pepper 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in the grated tomato and paprika, cooking 3-4 minutes until jammy and slightly darker.
Add the rice and stir 1-2 minutes to coat every grain in the sofrito.
Return the chicken to the pan, pour in the stock and saffron mixture, stir once to distribute evenly, then do not stir again.
Simmer uncovered over medium heat 10 minutes, then reduce to low and cook 8-10 minutes more, until the rice is nearly tender.
Nestle the shrimp into the rice and scatter the peas on top. Cook 5 minutes more until the shrimp are pink and opaque.
Raise the heat for the last 1-2 minutes to form a crispy bottom layer (the socarrat), listening for a light crackle.
Rest 5 minutes, covered loosely with foil, then serve straight from the pan with lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Tortilla Española (Spanish Potato Omelette)
recipes.dish_alt: A thick wedge of tortilla española with layers of tender potato and onion set in egg
recipes.prep_alt: Thinly sliced potatoes frying gently in olive oil, the classic first step of tortilla española

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Yukon gold or waxy potatoes, peeled, thin-sliced
Olive oil (for confit-frying, most drained off)

sections.heading: Steps
items: Peel and thinly slice the potatoes (about 3-4mm); thinly slice the onion.
Heat the olive oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Add the potatoes and onion, and season with salt.
Confit gently, stirring occasionally, 20-25 minutes, until the potatoes are fully tender but not browned.
Drain the potatoes and onion in a colander over a bowl, reserving the oil. Let cool 5 minutes.
Beat the eggs in a large bowl with a pinch of salt.
Fold the drained potato-onion mixture into the beaten eggs and let sit 5 minutes.
Heat 1-2 tablespoons of the reserved oil in a small nonstick skillet (18-20cm) over medium heat.
Pour in the egg-potato mixture, spreading evenly, and cook 2-3 minutes until the edges set.
Slide onto a plate, invert the pan over it, and flip both together so the tortilla drops back in uncooked-side down. Cook 2-3 minutes more, until just set but still soft in the center.
Slide onto a plate, rest 5 minutes, and slice into wedges to serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Gambas al Ajillo (Garlic Shrimp)
recipes.dish_alt: Sizzling gambas al ajillo, shrimp in golden garlic-chili olive oil, served in a small pan
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Raw Shrimp and Sliced Garlic
recipes.prep_alt: Raw peeled shrimp alongside thinly sliced garlic, ready for the hot oil

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Dried chili flakes (or ¼ dried guindilla)
Dry sherry or dry white wine

sections.heading: Steps
items: Pat the shrimp dry and season lightly with salt.
Combine the olive oil, sliced garlic, and chili flakes in a cold skillet.
Set over medium-low heat so the garlic warms gradually with the oil, 2-3 minutes, until fragrant and just turning golden — don't let it brown.
Raise the heat to medium-high and add the shrimp in a single layer.
Cook 1-2 minutes per side until the shrimp turn pink and opaque.
Pour in the sherry and let it bubble and reduce by about half, roughly 30 seconds.
Squeeze in the lemon juice and season with salt.
Remove from heat and sprinkle with chopped parsley.
Serve immediately, still sizzling in the pan, with crusty bread for dipping.

recipes.title: Pollo al Ajillo (Garlic Chicken)
recipes.dish_alt: Golden braised chicken pieces in a garlicky white wine sauce, pollo al ajillo
recipes.prep_label: Prep — A Generous Handful of Peeled Garlic
recipes.prep_alt: A pile of whole peeled garlic cloves, the defining ingredient of pollo al ajillo

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Bone-in chicken thighs, cut into pieces

sections.heading: Steps
items: Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat.
Brown the chicken skin-side down 5-6 minutes until deep golden, then flip and brown the other side 4-5 minutes. Remove to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium-low and add the whole garlic cloves to the same pan.
Cook the garlic gently 3-4 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden and softened but not burnt.
Pour in the white wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Return the chicken to the pan with the bay leaf and thyme; bring to a simmer.
Cover partway and simmer 15-18 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink near the bone.
Uncover and simmer 2-3 minutes more to reduce the sauce slightly.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve with crusty bread or roasted potatoes.

recipes.title: Albóndigas en Salsa (Spanish Meatballs in Tomato Sauce)
recipes.dish_alt: A cazuela of Spanish meatballs simmered in a rich tomato, onion, and garlic sofrito sauce
recipes.prep_alt: Ground meat and seasonings ready to be rolled into meatballs for albóndigas

sections.heading: Steps
items: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 5 minutes until softened.
Combine the ground beef, pork, soaked breadcrumbs, egg, garlic, grated onion, parsley, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper. Mix gently until just combined.
Roll into golf-ball-sized meatballs and chill 15-30 minutes to firm up.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet and brown the meatballs in batches, 2-3 minutes per side, until golden all over. Remove to a plate.
In the same pan, cook the diced onion 4-5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and roasted red pepper, cooking 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in the white wine and let it reduce by half, scraping up any browned bits.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, stock, and bay leaf; bring to a simmer.
Return the meatballs to the sauce, cover partway, and simmer 20-25 minutes, until cooked through and the sauce has thickened.
Taste, adjust the salt, discard the bay leaf, and serve with crusty bread or over rice.

recipes.title: Fabada Asturiana (Bean & Chorizo Stew)
recipes.dish_alt: A rustic bowl of fabada asturiana, creamy white beans with chorizo, morcilla, and tocino
recipes.prep_alt: A package of chorizo, morcilla, and tocino, the traditional compango that flavors fabada

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Dried large white beans (fabes), soaked overnight

sections.heading: Steps
items: Soak the dried beans in plenty of cold water overnight, at least 8 hours; drain before cooking.
Put the soaked beans in a large pot with the chorizo, tocino, whole garlic cloves, onion, and bay leaf.
Cover generously with cold stock and bring slowly to a bare simmer — never let it boil hard, or the bean skins split.
Skim off any foam that rises to the top.

Stir in the saffron and smoked paprika, partially cover, and simmer very gently 1.5-2 hours, until the beans are completely tender and creamy, adding a splash of cold water if it threatens to boil too hard.
About 20 minutes before the beans are done, add the morcilla so it doesn't fall apart from overcooking.
Once tender, lift out the chorizo, morcilla, and tocino, slice, and return to the pot.
Season the broth with salt to taste — it should be thick enough to lightly coat a spoon.
Let the stew rest off the heat 10 minutes before serving.
Ladle into bowls with beans, broth, and a bit of each meat, plus crusty bread on the side.

recipes.title: Patatas Bravas with Alioli (Dinner Combo, with Crusty Bread)
recipes.dish_alt: Crisp fried potato cubes topped with smoky red brava sauce and a swirl of garlic alioli
recipes.prep_alt: Garlic being crushed in a traditional mortar and pestle to start the alioli

sections.heading: Potato & Brava Sauce Ingredients by Serving
rows: Yukon gold or russet potatoes, 2cm cubes

sections.heading: Steps
items: Soak the cubed potatoes in cold water 20-30 minutes, then drain and pat completely dry.
Fry or roast the potatoes (220°C/425°F), turning occasionally, 20-25 minutes, until deeply golden and crisp outside, tender inside.
Meanwhile, warm olive oil in a saucepan, add the onion, and cook 4-5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, cook 1 minute, then stir in the smoked paprika and cayenne, cooking 30 seconds to bloom the spices.
Add the crushed tomatoes and simmer 10-12 minutes until thickened; stir in the sherry vinegar and season with salt.
For the alioli, whisk the minced garlic with the egg yolk and a pinch of salt.
Whisking constantly, add the oil in a thin, slow stream, then a bit faster once thickened, until glossy and mayonnaise-like.
Whisk in the lemon juice and season with salt to taste.
Drain the crisped potatoes and pile onto a plate.
Spoon the warm brava sauce over the potatoes, drizzle with alioli, and serve with crusty bread as a full dinner plate.

recipes.title: Crema Catalana (Bonus)
recipes.dish_alt: Crema catalana with a crackly, deep amber caramelized sugar crust in a shallow terracotta dish
recipes.prep_alt: A kitchen torch caramelizing a layer of sugar into a crisp, amber crust over chilled custard

sections.heading: Steps
items: Pour the milk into a saucepan with the lemon peel, orange peel, and cinnamon stick.
Warm gently until steaming but not boiling, then remove from heat and steep 10-15 minutes. Strain out the peels and cinnamon.
Whisk the egg yolks with the sugar until pale, then whisk in the cornstarch until smooth.
Slowly pour a little of the warm milk into the yolk mixture, whisking constantly to temper the eggs.
Pour the tempered mixture back into the saucepan with the rest of the milk.
Cook over low heat, whisking constantly, 5-8 minutes, until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Pour into shallow ramekins or terracotta dishes and cool to room temperature.
Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours, until fully chilled and set.
Just before serving, sprinkle an even layer of sugar over each custard.
Caramelize with a kitchen torch (or hot broiler for 1-2 minutes) until deep amber and crackly, then serve immediately.
